title: Customer Security Questionnaire Handling
heading: 1. Intake
text:
# Customer Security Questionnaire Handling

Enterprise customers often send security questionnaires before they sign or renew. This process describes how DSEC answers them accurately and quickly. Sales and Support bring the request to us; we own the answers.

## 1. Intake

1. The account team opens a request in the DSEC intake queue and attaches the questionnaire, the customer name, and the deadline.
2. A compliance analyst on the rota acknowledges within one business day and becomes the coordinator.
3. The coordinator reads the questionnaire and sorts the questions into topics: identity, development, data handling, availability, and certifications.

title: Customer Security Questionnaire Handling
heading: 2. The answer library
text:
## 2. The answer library

We keep a library of approved answers in Confluence. Each entry has an owner, a last-reviewed date, and a link to the source document for the claim.

- Reuse library answers wherever they fit the question.
- Do not paraphrase an answer in a way that changes its meaning.
- If a question has no library answer, route it to the owning team (see below) and add the new answer to the library once it is approved.

title: Customer Security Questionnaire Handling
heading: 3. Who answers what
text:
## 3. Who answers what

| Topic | Route to |
|---|---|
| Single sign-on and identity | IT & Compliance |
| Code scanning and secrets | AppSec |
| Data lake and event data | Data Platform |
| Machine learning systems | ML Infrastructure |
| Availability and recovery | SRE guild |
| Legal and contract terms | Legal |

Owning teams answer within three business days and cite the source document.

title: Customer Security Questionnaire Handling
heading: 4. Certifications and reports
text:
## 4. Certifications and reports

TechSync holds SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certifications. Customers can receive the current SOC 2 report and the ISO certificate under a non-disclosure agreement. The coordinator requests them through the CISO's office; do not send reports directly.

title: Customer Security Questionnaire Handling
heading: 5. Review and sending
text:
## 5. Review and sending

1. The coordinator assembles the answers and checks them for consistency.
2. A Security Engineer reviews anything about technical controls.
3. The CISO's office approves answers that make new commitments.
4. The account team sends the response, not DSEC.

title: Customer Security Questionnaire Handling
heading: 6. Commitments
text:
## 6. Commitments

If a customer asks us to commit to something we do not already do, such as a bespoke contractual term, it is not answered here. Escalate it to Legal and the VP.

## 7. After the response

- Save the final questionnaire and answers on the request ticket.
- Update the library with any new approved answers.
- Note recurring questions in the monthly review; they are candidates for a public trust page.

title: Annual Audit Preparation Calendar
heading: Annual Audit Preparation Calendar
text:
# Annual Audit Preparation Calendar

TechSync is audited each year against SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001. This calendar shows the milestones for the compliance team and the DSEC engineers who supply evidence, so that audit season is a series of small steps rather than a scramble.

title: Annual Audit Preparation Calendar
heading: How the year is organized
text:
## How the year is organized

| Period | Focus |
|---|---|
| January to February | Close out last year's findings; refresh the control mapping |
| March | Kick off the SOC 2 observation review; assign evidence owners |
| April to May | Evidence collection and gap checks |
| June | Auditor fieldwork for SOC 2 Type II |
| July | Respond to auditor questions; remediation of any gaps |
| August | SOC 2 report issued; lessons-learned session |
| September | ISO 27001 surveillance audit preparation |
| October | ISO 27001 surveillance audit |
| November | Remediation of ISO findings |
| December | Planning for next year; control owner review |

Dates move by a few weeks each year depending on the auditors' schedule. The compliance team posts the exact dates in the compliance channel in January.

title: Annual Audit Preparation Calendar
heading: What engineers are asked to do
text:
## What engineers are asked to do

1. **Confirm control ownership.** Each control in Compass has an owning team. Owners check their list in March.
2. **Provide evidence when asked.** The Compliance Evidence Handbook explains the format and how to upload to Compass.
3. **Respond to gap tickets within five business days.** The weekly gap check opens tickets when evidence is missing.
4. **Be available during fieldwork.** Auditors may ask an engineer to walk through how a control works. The compliance analyst will brief you beforehand.

title: Annual Audit Preparation Calendar
heading: What the compliance team does
text:
## What the compliance team does

- Maintains the control mapping and the evidence tracker.
- Runs the weekly gap check during evidence collection.
- Coordinates all communication with the auditors.
- Reports status to the CISO.

## Tips for evidence owners

- Collect evidence as work happens, not at the end.
- Name files so someone else can find them.
- If you are unsure whether something counts, ask the analyst before the deadline.

## Contacts

The compliance channel, or the analyst assigned to your team on the evidence plan.

title: DSEC Terraform Module Conventions
heading: 1. Repository layout
text:
# DSEC Terraform Module Conventions

DSEC teams manage their infrastructure with Terraform. These conventions keep modules readable and reusable across the four teams.

## 1. Repository layout

```
modules/
  <module-name>/
    main.tf
    variables.tf
    outputs.tf
    README.md
environments/
  dev/
  staging/
  prod/
```

Each environment folder contains only module calls and environment-specific values.

title: DSEC Terraform Module Conventions
heading: 2. Naming
text:
## 2. Naming

- Resources use `snake_case` names that describe their role: `reservoir_raw_bucket`, not `bucket1`.
- Variables and outputs are described in `variables.tf` and `outputs.tf`; every one has a description.
- Module names are nouns: `kafka_topic`, `s3_bucket`, `keystone_app`.

title: DSEC Terraform Module Conventions
heading: 3. Versioning
text:
## 3. Versioning

Modules are versioned with tags (`v1.2.0`). Environments pin a version. Breaking changes bump the major version and are announced in the DSEC channel.

## 4. State

State lives in S3 with locking, one state per environment per component. Never share a state file between teams.

title: DSEC Terraform Module Conventions
heading: 5. Secrets
text:
## 5. Secrets

Do not put secrets in variables or in version control. Reference them through the Vaultline data sources and mark sensitive outputs as `sensitive`.

## 6. Review and apply

1. Open a pull request. CI runs `terraform fmt`, `validate`, and `plan`.
2. A teammate reviews the plan output, not just the code.
3. Apply to dev and staging from the pipeline. Prod applies require approval from the team's tech lead.

title: DSEC Terraform Module Conventions
heading: 7. Tags
text:
## 7. Tags

Every resource carries `owner_team`, `service`, and `environment` tags so costs and ownership are visible.

## 8. Deprecating modules

Announce at least one release cycle ahead and keep the old version available for that time.

title: DSEC Internal Request Intake
heading: One front door
text:
# DSEC Internal Request Intake

How to ask a DSEC team for something, and what happens next.

## One front door

All requests from outside DSEC, and most from inside, go through the DSEC intake queue in Jira. Do not send requests by direct message; they are easy to lose, and a ticket gives you a place to track progress.

title: DSEC Internal Request Intake
heading: What to put in a request
text:
## What to put in a request

1. A one-line summary.
2. What you need, and why.
3. Who is affected and by when it matters.
4. Links to related tickets, documents, or incidents.
5. Which system it concerns, if you know.

title: DSEC Internal Request Intake
heading: Request types
text:
## Request types

| Type | Examples |
|---|---|
| Access | Group membership, vault paths, GPU quota |
| Advice | Design consultation, security questions |
| Change | A feature in a DSEC system |
| Docs | A missing or incorrect document |
| Incident follow-up | A fix coming out of a postmortem |

Urgent operational problems are not requests. Page the owning team through Lookout or use the team's on-call channel.

title: DSEC Internal Request Intake
heading: Triage
text:
## Triage

An intake rota of engineering managers reviews the queue each business day. They:

- Confirm the request is clear, or ask for detail.
- Route it to the owning team.
- Set a priority from P1 to P4.

The owning team then schedules the work in its own planning process.

title: DSEC Internal Request Intake
heading: Priorities
text:
## Priorities

| Priority | Meaning |
|---|---|
| P1 | Blocks a launch or many people |
| P2 | Blocks one team |
| P3 | Useful, can wait |
| P4 | Nice to have |

title: DSEC Internal Request Intake
heading: Tracking and closing
text:
## Tracking and closing

The assignee comments when work starts and when it finishes. Requesters should confirm that the result works before the ticket is closed.

## If a request is stuck

Comment on the ticket first. If there is no response, raise it in the DSEC channel and mention the owning team's engineering manager.

title: DSEC H1 2026 Retrospective
heading: DSEC H1 2026 Retrospective
text:
# DSEC H1 2026 Retrospective

**Date:** 14 Jul 2026 | **Facilitator:** TPM | **Present:** the four engineering managers, four tech leads, and about 25 engineers

We used the usual format: what went well, what did not, and what we will try. Sticky notes were clustered by theme; this is the summary.

title: DSEC H1 2026 Retrospective
heading: What went well
text:
## What went well

**Cross-team delivery**
- The Foundry autoscaling change landed with help from Platform Engineering, and several people said it was the smoothest cross-org effort of the half.
- The SBOM build step reached most Scaffold-based repositories ahead of the plan.
- The Keystone directory sync work finished with fewer escalations than we had feared.

**Documentation**
- Runbooks written alongside new systems were noticed by on-call engineers. A few people called out the Streamline playbooks as a model.
- The landing page made finding documents easier.

**People**
- New joiners reported that the onboarding guide and their buddies made the first month easier than at previous companies.

title: DSEC H1 2026 Retrospective
heading: What did not go well
text:
## What did not go well

**Planning**
- Late changes to the quarterly plan caused churn for two teams.
- Dependencies on other orgs were discovered late, mostly during the build rather than the plan.

**Operations**
- One serving latency incident showed that alerts did not cover slow-but-healthy endpoints.
- A scanning queue backlog in June slowed developers for a day.

**Communication**
- Some teams learned about interface changes from a failing job rather than an announcement.

title: DSEC H1 2026 Retrospective
heading: Themes and what we will try
text:
## Themes and what we will try

| Theme | Experiment | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Late dependencies | Review dependency table in week -2, not week -1 | TPM |
| Interface changes | Announce breaking changes in the DSEC channel two weeks ahead | Tech leads |
| Alert coverage | Add a "how would we notice a slow failure?" question to design reviews | Staff engineers |
| Plan churn | Lock the plan after week 0 except through the planning doc | Engineering managers |

title: DSEC H1 2026 Retrospective
heading: Shout-outs
text:
## Shout-outs

Thanks to the SRE who drove the rollout gate changes, to the compliance analysts for their work through the audit season, and to the staff engineer who mentored three new joiners.

## Next retro

The next retrospective will cover Q3 and Q4 together.

title: Access Review Policy
heading: 1. Policy statement
text:
# Access Review Policy

**Owner:** IT & Compliance | **Applies to:** all TechSync employees, contractors, and systems

## 1. Policy statement

TechSync reviews who has access to its systems **every quarter**. This policy takes effect in February 2024; the first quarterly cycle opens in April 2024.

title: Access Review Policy
heading: 2. Scope
text:
## 2. Scope

All systems that hold production access, customer-derived data, or administrative privileges are in scope. This includes services of every tier: Tier 0 core platform, Tier 1 customer-facing, Tier 2 internal, and **Tier 3 experimental**. Being a Tier 3 service does not exempt it from review.

title: Access Review Policy
heading: 3. Cycle
text:
## 3. Cycle

- Review cycles open on the first business day of January, April, July, and October.
- Each reviewer has 15 business days to complete their review.
- IT & Compliance generates the review lists from Keystone group and entitlement exports.

title: Access Review Policy
heading: 4. Responsibilities
text:
## 4. Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| System owner | Confirms every account and entitlement is still needed |
| Reviewing manager | Confirms access for their direct reports |
| IT & Compliance | Opens cycles, chases overdue reviews, reports completion |
| CISO | Receives the completion report each cycle |

title: Access Review Policy
heading: 5. Revocation
text:
## 5. Revocation

Access marked as no longer needed must be removed within 2 business days of the decision.

## 6. Evidence

**Evidence of every completed review must be uploaded to Compass**, for every in-scope system, Tier 3 included. Evidence consists of the exported access list, the reviewer's decisions, and the ticket showing removals. Reviews with no evidence in Compass are treated as not completed.

title: Access Review Policy
heading: 7. Escalation
text:
## 7. Escalation

Reviews not finished by the end of the window are escalated to the reviewer's engineering manager, and then to the CISO, Tamsin Reid.

## 8. Audit

The completed-review records in Compass are provided to our SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 auditors on request.

title: Access Review Policy v1
heading: Access Review Policy v1
text:
> **DEPRECATED (February 2024).** This version is outdated. It was replaced by CO-DSEC-001, Access Review Policy, and is retained for audit history only. Do not follow it.

# Access Review Policy v1

**Owner:** IT & Compliance | **Applies to:** all TechSync employees and contractors

title: Access Review Policy v1
heading: 1. Policy statement
text:
## 1. Policy statement

Access to TechSync production systems is reviewed **twice a year, in January and July**.

## 2. Cycle

- Review cycles open on the first business day of January and July.
- Each reviewer has 20 business days to complete their review.
- IT & Compliance generates review lists from Keystone group exports.

title: Access Review Policy v1
heading: 3. Responsibilities
text:
## 3. Responsibilities

System owners confirm that each account is still needed. Managers confirm access for their direct reports. IT & Compliance chases overdue reviews and reports completion to the CISO.

## 4. Revocation

Access marked as no longer needed is removed within 5 business days.

## 5. Evidence

Completed review records are stored in Compass for the audit team.

title: Vulnerability Remediation SLA Policy
heading: 1. Policy
text:
# Vulnerability Remediation SLA Policy

**Owner:** AppSec | **Effective:** November 2024 | **Applies to:** all engineering teams

## 1. Policy

Vulnerabilities in TechSync services and their dependencies must be fixed within the following times:

| Severity | Fix within |
|---|---|
| Critical | 7 days |
| High | 30 days |

Medium and Low findings are handled in each team's regular backlog review and have no fixed deadline.

title: Vulnerability Remediation SLA Policy
heading: 2. When the clock starts
text:
## 2. When the clock starts

The clock starts when Sentinel, a pen test report, or a bug bounty report confirms the finding. If a finding is disputed, the clock keeps running until AppSec records the dispute as resolved.

## 3. What "fixed" means

A finding is fixed when the vulnerable code or dependency is no longer present in production, or when a verified mitigation has been deployed and AppSec has accepted it in the ticket.

title: Vulnerability Remediation SLA Policy
heading: 4. Responsibilities
text:
## 4. Responsibilities

- **Service owners** triage within one business day, plan the fix, and ship it.
- **AppSec** confirms severity, verifies fixes, and reports SLA performance monthly.
- **Engineering managers** are accountable for overdue findings in their teams.

title: Vulnerability Remediation SLA Policy
heading: 5. Extensions
text:
## 5. Extensions

An extension needs written approval from AppSec with a compensating control and a new due date. Critical findings can only be extended by the CISO.

## 6. Reporting

AppSec publishes a monthly dashboard showing open findings, age, and breaches by team. Repeated breaches are reviewed with the VP of the owning org.

title: Secrets Rotation Policy
heading: 1. Policy
text:
# Secrets Rotation Policy

**Owner:** AppSec | **Effective:** January 2025

## 1. Policy

**Secrets are rotated every 90 days.** This interval shortens the previous 180-day rule, and all secrets must meet it from the effective date.

title: Secrets Rotation Policy
heading: 2. Scope
text:
## 2. Scope

The policy covers long-lived secrets managed in Vaultline or stored in any other system:

- Service API keys
- Database passwords
- Signing keys and tokens
- Integration credentials for third parties

Short-lived credentials issued by Vaultline with automatic leases are governed by the Vaultline runbooks, not by this policy.

title: Secrets Rotation Policy
heading: 3. Responsibilities
text:
## 3. Responsibilities

- **Service owners** rotate their secrets and confirm each rotation in Vaultline.
- **AppSec** reports any secret older than the interval in the monthly review.
- **Engineering managers** are accountable for overdue secrets in their teams.

title: Secrets Rotation Policy
heading: 4. Process
text:
## 4. Process

1. Vaultline sends a reminder 14 days before the interval ends.
2. The owner creates the new secret and deploys it alongside the old one.
3. After verification, the old secret is revoked.
4. The rotation date is recorded in Vaultline metadata.

## 5. Exceptions

A secret that cannot be rotated on schedule needs a written exception from AppSec with a compensating control and an end date.

## 1. Policy

title: Log, Trace and Dataset Retention Policy
heading: 1. Policy
text:
# Log, Trace and Dataset Retention Policy

**Owner:** Data Platform (DATA) | **Effective:** January 2026

## 1. Policy

Logs, traces, and dataset archives are kept **30 days hot and 13 months in archive**. After the archive period ends, the data is deleted.

| Data | Hot storage | Archive |
|---|---|---|
| Logs | 30 days | 13 months |
| Traces | 30 days | 13 months |
| Dataset archives | 30 days | 13 months |

title: Log, Trace and Dataset Retention Policy
heading: 2. Definitions
text:
## 2. Definitions

- **Hot:** immediately queryable at full performance. For logs and traces this is OpenSearch-backed storage; for datasets it is the active Reservoir tier.
- **Archive:** compressed storage on S3 that can be restored on request. Restores take up to several hours.

title: Log, Trace and Dataset Retention Policy
heading: 3. Scope
text:
## 3. Scope

The policy covers every product and internal system that emits logs or traces, and every dataset registered in Reservoir. It applies in all regions. EU customer data stays in eu-west-1, in both hot and archive tiers.

title: Log, Trace and Dataset Retention Policy
heading: 4. Responsibilities
text:
## 4. Responsibilities

- **Data Platform** operates the lifecycle jobs that move data from hot to archive and delete expired data.
- **Observability and product teams** configure their pipelines to use the standard tiers and must not set longer values.
- **Service owners** are responsible for data in their own services' pipelines.

title: Log, Trace and Dataset Retention Policy
heading: 5. Legal holds
text:
## 5. Legal holds

Legal can place a hold on specific data. Held data is excluded from deletion until Legal releases the hold. Requests go through the CISO's office.

## 6. Restoring from archive

1. Open a ticket in the DATA queue with the data set, time range, and reason.
2. DATA confirms the classification and approves the restore.
3. The restore completes in the requested scratch location and is deleted after use.

title: Log, Trace and Dataset Retention Policy
heading: 7. Auditing
text:
## 7. Auditing

Lifecycle job runs are logged and sampled monthly by IT & Compliance. Evidence is stored in Compass for SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001.

## 8. Changes

Requests to change retention values go to the Data Platform engineering manager and the CISO.

title: Production Access Policy
heading: 1. Policy
text:
# Production Access Policy

**Owner:** IT & Compliance | **Effective:** October 2025 | **Applies to:** every person and automated agent that signs in to production systems

## 1. Policy

**A hardware security key is required for production access.** Authenticator apps and SMS codes are not accepted for any production sign-in.

title: Production Access Policy
heading: 2. What counts as a hardware security key
text:
## 2. What counts as a hardware security key

A FIDO2/WebAuthn-compliant physical key, issued by IT or purchased from the approved vendor list. Platform keys built into laptops are not a substitute for production access.

title: Production Access Policy
heading: 3. Enrollment
text:
## 3. Enrollment

1. Request a key through the IT helpdesk, or use your own from the approved list.
2. Register it in Keystone under Security settings.
3. Register a second key as a backup. IT recommends keeping it in a separate location.
4. Complete a test sign-in to a production console before your current access expires.

title: Production Access Policy
heading: 4. Lost or damaged keys
text:
## 4. Lost or damaged keys

Report the loss to the IT helpdesk immediately. IT revokes the key in Keystone, and your backup key keeps your access working. If both are lost, a manager must confirm your identity before a temporary replacement is issued.

title: Production Access Policy
heading: 5. Break-glass access
text:
## 5. Break-glass access

Break-glass accounts are held by the SRE guild. They also use hardware keys, kept in the sealed safe in the Denver office, and every use triggers a page to the CISO's office.

title: Production Access Policy
heading: 6. Responsibilities
text:
## 6. Responsibilities

- **Individuals:** keep keys safe and never share them.
- **Engineering managers:** make sure new starters in production roles enroll before their first on-call shift.
- **IT & Compliance:** operate enrollment, maintain the approved vendor list, report coverage monthly.

## 7. Exceptions

There are no standing exceptions. Short-term accommodations, for example for accessibility needs, are approved by the CISO and documented in Keystone.

title: Production Access Policy v1
heading: 1. Policy
text:
## 1. Policy

Multi-factor authentication is required for production access. **An authenticator app (time-based one-time passwords) is acceptable.** SMS codes are not accepted.

## 2. Enrollment

## 3. Lost devices

## 4. Break-glass

title: Data Classification Standard
heading: 1. Levels
text:
# Data Classification Standard

**Owner:** Office of the CISO | **Applies to:** all TechSync data in any system

## 1. Levels

TechSync classifies data into four levels.

| Level | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Public | Approved for release outside the company |
| Internal | For employees and contractors; not for release |
| Confidential | Sensitive business or customer information |
| Restricted | The most sensitive data, with the tightest handling |

title: Data Classification Standard
heading: 2. Default classification
text:
## 2. Default classification

**Customer-derived data is Confidential by default.** This covers data that customers send to our products and data computed from it, such as usage records, logs that contain customer content, and aggregated customer metrics.

**Restricted is reserved for credentials, payment card data, and regulated identifiers.**

title: Data Classification Standard
heading: 3. Handling by level
text:
## 3. Handling by level

| Requirement | Internal | Confidential | Restricted |
|---|---|---|---|
| Encryption at rest | Yes | Yes | Yes, with dedicated keys |
| Encryption in transit | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Access | All employees | Need-to-know group | Named individuals |
| Storage outside approved AWS regions | Not allowed | Not allowed | Not allowed |
| Sharing with third parties | Contract needed | Contract and review | Not permitted without CISO approval |

title: Data Classification Standard
heading: 4. Labelling
text:
## 4. Labelling

Datasets registered in Reservoir, tables in Quarry, and buckets in Terraform carry a `classification` tag. Untagged assets are treated as Confidential until reviewed.

## 5. Declassification

Moving data to a lower level requires the data owner and a Security Engineer to sign off in a Jira ticket.

## 6. Questions

Contact the compliance channel. Disputes on classification go to the CISO, Tamsin Reid.

title: Open-Source License Policy
heading: 1. Policy
text:
# Open-Source License Policy

**Owner:** AppSec, with Legal | **Applies to:** all code, libraries, and tools used at TechSync, in products and in internal tooling

## 1. Policy

Only open-source software under an **approved license** may be used. **Copyleft-licensed software requires legal review** before first use. This applies whether or not the software will ever be distributed outside the company.

title: Open-Source License Policy
heading: 2. Approved licenses
text:
## 2. Approved licenses

- MIT
- Apache License 2.0
- BSD 2-Clause and 3-Clause
- ISC

Components under any license not on this list are not approved until reviewed.

## 3. Copyleft

Licenses in the GPL family (GPL, LGPL, AGPL) and other strong copyleft licenses need a legal review. Open a request through AppSec; AppSec routes it to Legal. Do not merge code that depends on the library until the review is granted.

title: Open-Source License Policy
heading: 4. How Sentinel helps
text:
## 4. How Sentinel helps

Sentinel detects licenses in dependencies and flags anything not on the approved list on the pull request. Flagged dependencies need either a swap to an approved alternative or a legal review request.

## 5. Records

AppSec keeps an inventory of all approved reviews. Each entry names the library, version, intended use, and reviewer.

## 6. Exceptions

Exceptions to this policy must be approved in writing by the CISO and Legal and must state their scope.

title: Information Security Policy Framework Overview
heading: How the policy set is organized
text:
# Information Security Policy Framework Overview

This page explains how TechSync's information security policies fit together and where to find each one. It deliberately contains no requirements; each policy states its own.

## How the policy set is organized

The framework has three layers:

1. **Company-wide policies** apply to every employee and contractor. The CISO's office sponsors them, and each has a named owning team.
2. **Org-wide standards** describe how an org applies company policies in its own work.
3. **Team runbooks and guides** explain how a team operates its own systems.

When you need an answer, start at the most specific layer that applies to you, then check the layers above it for anything your team must follow.

title: Information Security Policy Framework Overview
heading: Who owns what
text:
## Who owns what

| Policy area | Owning function |
|---|---|
| Access reviews | IT & Compliance |
| Production access | IT & Compliance |
| Vulnerability remediation | AppSec |
| Secrets rotation | AppSec |
| Open-source licenses | Legal, through AppSec |
| Data classification | Office of the CISO |
| Log, trace and dataset retention | Data Platform |

title: Information Security Policy Framework Overview
heading: Where documents live
text:
## Where documents live

Policies are published in Confluence under the Security space. Approved versions carry an owner and a last-reviewed date. Older versions are archived and marked so that audit history is complete.

## How policies change

1. The owning team drafts the change and opens a review ticket.
2. Stakeholders from affected teams comment for two weeks.
3. The CISO approves.
4. The Technical Writing group publishes the new version and announces it in Slack.

title: Information Security Policy Framework Overview
heading: Audit and assurance
text:
## Audit and assurance

TechSync maintains SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certifications, and IT & Compliance maps each policy to the relevant controls in Compass.

## Getting help

Ask in the compliance channel, or contact the owning team listed above.
